title: Local constancy of the sheaf of integral lattices
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, and let $A=\mathcal O_E$ be its valuation ring with the induced $\ell$-adic topology [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. On $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] use the coefficient ring sheaves $A_X(V)=C(|V|,A)$ and $E_X(V)=C(|V|,E)$ of continuous functions. Let $L$ be an $E_X$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] locally free of finite rank: some pro-etale covering trivializes it to finite sums of $E$, with ranks allowed to vary. For $U\to X$ define $\mathscr L_L(U)$ to be the set of isomorphism classes of pairs $(M,\alpha)$, where $M$ is an $A_U$-module sheaf pro-etale locally free of finite rank and $\alpha:E_U\otimes_{A_U}M\xrightarrow{\sim}L|_U$ is an $E_U$-linear isomorphism [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Two pairs are identified exactly when an $A_U$-linear isomorphism between their modules intertwines their maps $\alpha$; restriction is inverse image on the localized site [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. This presheaf is a sheaf of sets. If $L|_U\cong E_U^n$ for $n\geq0$, then $\mathscr L_L|_U\cong\underline{S_n}_U$, where $S_n=\operatorname{GL}_n(E)/\operatorname{GL}_n(A)$ is the set of cosets $g\operatorname{GL}_n(A)$, namely the orbits for right multiplication by $\operatorname{GL}_n(A)$, $\operatorname{GL}_n(R)$ is the group of invertible $n$ by $n$ matrices over $R$, and $\underline{S_n}_U$ is the sheafification of the constant presheaf with value the discrete set $S_n$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. The isomorphism sends $g\operatorname{GL}_n(A)$ to $(gA_U^n,\alpha_g)$, with $\alpha_g$ the scalar-extension isomorphism induced by the inclusion into $E_U^n$.

proof.text: Apply the exact descent/presentation theorem, obtaining F,c and the three presentation clauses. This is the global class-descent part only; it asserts neither local constancy nor a coset isomorphism. Foundational declarations are reexported from LatticeSheafBasic without changing their signatures.

For each rational frame use the normalized constant-coset map. Its local injectivity is proved by image classification and point evaluation, including the empty-cover case. Its local surjectivity follows from finite local bases, continuous matrix frames and open constant-coset neighborhoods.

The locally bijective presheaf map induces an isomorphism of set sheaves in the required large universe. Take its asIso and use the proved normalization theorem to identify the action on every constant coset. The original finite-local-freeness hypothesis is retained; the argument works on any specified rational frame.

All coset, neighborhood, cover, integral continuous lifting, local-bijectivity, sheafification and normalization glue is proved. No unit route is bypassed. Foundational definitions and the previously proved four auxiliary nodes move to LatticeSheafBasic solely to allow acyclic proof imports.

lean.note: Uses an exact quotient presentation: sections are covered by actual lattice pairs with equality precisely intertwining integral isomorphism; all restriction maps are characterized by embedded images on slice objects. The constant-coset isomorphism is normalized on every constant matrix. WithAbs transports the recorded valuation subring to its canonical absolute-value topology; no topology assumption or rank bound is added. Helpers belong to the constructions explicitly introduced in this node. The commutative continuous-coefficient presentation generalizes the upstream RingCat-only, Type-zero coefficient construction to coefficients in the scheme universe. B3: all former foundational declarations live in the publicly imported LatticeSheafBasic with unchanged signatures and definitions; see its four attached auxiliary nodes and the interface change record.

statement_change.what: The words "right cosets" were ambiguous relative to the explicit formula g GL_n(A). Standard group terminology and Mathlib call gH left cosets; the actual source map g to g A^n identifies the orbits of RIGHT multiplication, namely gH, rather than Hg. Clarify that exact quotient without changing any hypothesis or formula. For the literal Hg convention the prescribed map is not well defined: in rank two take g = diag(l,1) and h = [[1,1],[0,1]] in GL_2(A). Then g and hg have the same Hg coset, but hg A^2 contains (1,1), which is not in g A^2 because l is a nonunit of A.

old_proof.text: Associate to $(M,\alpha)$ the map $j_M:M\to L|_U$, $m\mapsto\alpha(1\otimes m)$. It is injective: locally $M=A^r$, and the natural map $A_V^r\to E_V^r$ is the coordinatewise inclusion of continuous functions. The free-module tensor isomorphism sends $e\otimes(a_i)$ to $(ea_i)$, with inverse $(e_i)\mapsto\sum_i e_i\otimes b_i$ for the coordinate basis $b_i$. A section killed by $j_M$ is zero on a covering and thus zero by separatedness. Regard $M$ as an embedded submodule of $L$. An intertwining isomorphism of pairs is unique, since its composite with injective $j_N$ must equal $j_M$. Two pairs are equivalent exactly when their embedded submodule sheaves agree.

old_proof.text: For a covering $(U_i\to U)_i$ and a matching family of classes, choose representatives $(M_i,\alpha_i)$. Equality of classes on overlaps supplies unique intertwining isomorphisms $\phi_{ij}$. On triple overlaps, $\phi_{jk}\phi_{ij}$ and $\phi_{ik}$ intertwine the same rationalizations, so step 1 proves the cocycle. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-sheaf-gluing] on the slice over $U$ with ring sheaf $A_U$ to obtain $M$ and local isomorphisms $e_i:M|_{U_i}\cong M_i$. Composite refinements trivializing all the $M_i$ trivialize $M$, using the site covering axioms. Slice restrictions have the sectionwise coefficient and module structures of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site].

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), proof, pp. 59–60; explicit continuous-matrix form of the local calculation

old_proof.text: The maps $j_{M_i}e_i$ agree on overlaps. For any section of $M$ over $V\to U$, glue their images on $V\times_UU_i$ by the sheaf condition of $L$. Uniqueness makes this a natural $A_U$-linear map $j:M\to L|_U$. The bilinear rule $(e,m)\mapsto ej(m)$ induces $\alpha:E_U\otimes_{A_U}M\to L|_U$. Slice restriction commutes with this tensor: sectionwise tensors and coverings of slice objects are the same, so the sheafifications have identical local descriptions. Locally $\alpha$ is $\alpha_i$, and their inverse maps agree and glue sectionwise. Thus $\alpha$ is an isomorphism. For two amalgamations the unique intertwining local isomorphisms of step 1 agree on overlaps and glue; their inverses glue too. This proves unique amalgamation of classes and the sheaf property of $\mathscr L_L$.

old_proof.text: Fix $L|_U=E_U^n$. Every $g\in\operatorname{GL}_n(E)$ gives $gA_U^n\subset E_U^n$ with rationalization induced by inclusion. Multiplication by $g$ trivializes this integral module and its rationalization. Right multiplication by $h\in\operatorname{GL}_n(A)$ leaves the embedded module unchanged, giving a natural map from the constant presheaf $S_n$ to $\mathscr L_L|_U$. If two constant lattices agree over a nonempty object $V$, evaluate coordinate sections at any point of $V$. Every column of each matrix has continuous $A$-coordinates in the other, so the change matrix and its inverse have entries in $A$. The right cosets are equal. On an empty object use the empty covering. This is local injectivity.

old_proof.text: For any pair over $V\to U$, refine a pro-etale covering to choose a basis of $M$ on each nonempty member $T$. The rationalized basis and inverse of $\alpha$ give mutually inverse matrices between $E_T^r$ and $E_T^n$. Evaluation at a point gives $r=n$, since these matrices define inverse vector-space isomorphisms. The embedded lattice is therefore $gA_T^n$ for $g$ and $g^{-1}$ with entries in $E_T(T)=C(|T|,E)$. A linear map out of a finite free module sheaf is determined by the global coordinate sections, and every section is their coefficient-linear combination, so these matrices describe the maps on every slice object.

old_proof.text: For $t\in|T|$ put $g_t=g(t)$. Apply [lem-pod-lattice-stabilizer-open] with $E^n$ and the finitely generated spanning lattice $A^n$. Its stabilizer is $\operatorname{GL}_n(A)$, because preservation in both directions means that a matrix and its inverse have entries in $A$. Finite-dimensional evaluation at a basis identifies the compact-open linear-map topology with the matrix-entry topology: evaluation is continuous, and any compact set has bounded coordinates, so sufficiently small entry differences are uniformly small on it. Thus continuity of the entries of $g$ makes $W_t=\{s:g_t^{-1}g(s)\in\operatorname{GL}_n(A)\}$ an open neighborhood of $t$. On every object over $W_t$, the matrices $g_t^{-1}g$ and $g^{-1}g_t$ are inverse matrices with continuous $A$-valued entries (use the induced topology on $A$). They are inverse over its coefficient ring, so $gA^n|_{W_t}=g_tA_{W_t}^n$ as submodule sheaves. The opens $W_t$ cover $T$; [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and the covering-preserving inclusion in [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] make them a pro-etale covering. Composition with the basis covering proves local surjectivity of the constant-presheaf map.

old_proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], the map of step 4 extends uniquely to $\underline{S_n}_U\to\mathscr L_L|_U$. It is locally surjective by step 6. To prove local injectivity, [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] represents two source sections by constant cosets on a common covering refinement. If their images agree, step 4 makes these representatives equal on a further covering, so the source sections are locally equal. Apply [lem-galois-set-sheaf-local-bijection-isomorphism] to obtain the isomorphism, with the stated action on constant cosets. For $n=0$ there is one coset and only the zero pair. For an empty scheme the empty-cover sheaf axiom gives the unique section. The original covering trivializing $L$ therefore witnesses local constancy with the allowed varying ranks.
